The "notorious malevolent forces" blamed by Emre Tezmen for the collapse of his financial empire were not a specific group of conspirators. Instead, as the video concludes, the collapse was driven by market forces—specifically, the sellers (32:44 - 33:04).

Tezmen had constructed a "perpetual motion machine" (4:36) where his funds purchased their own affiliated stocks to artificially inflate valuations. This system required a constant inflow of new capital and relied on the assumption that nobody would ever sell their holdings. When the regulator finally intervened, or when retail investors began to lose confidence and attempted to withdraw their money, the system faced a liquidity spiral (13:36 - 13:58). As prices fell, the funds were forced to sell their illiquid assets at a discount, which drove prices down further and rendered the funds unable to meet redemption requests.

Throughout the investigation, several parties were accused or scrutinized, but none were the actual "malevolent forces":

Whistleblowers: Like Ramazan Basak, who were detained for questioning the feasibility of the massive returns (10:22 - 11:12).
Regulators: Whose eventual rules against concentrated holdings finally caused the bubble to burst (18:34 - 19:10).
Retail Investors: Like the 28-year-old trying to pay for a wedding, who were simply trying to access their own savings (13:58 - 14:37).
MSCI: Whose warnings about market manipulation pressured the regulator into taking action (24:40 - 26:15).
